 Judgment
This is a suit filed by the plaintiff against the defendants for the relief of permanent injunction and costs.

2. The brief facts as averred in the plaint are that:-
The plaintiff is a physically handicapped person and running a small petty shop in the suit schedule property since past 20 years under the name and style of Sri.Maruthi Condiment Shop, situated at Konanakunte Cross, Near Bus Stop, Kanakapura Main Road, Bangalore, measuring 6 x 9 feet, morefully described in the suit schedule.

He has availed loan for Petty Retailer of Snacks / Tea Shop from Syndicate Bank,
Doddakalasandra Branch, Bangalore, for an amount of Rs.3,00,000/- through SC/ST Scheme and also obtained subsidy from the said loan.
The plaintiff submits that he has been paying monthly EMI to the bank from the earning of the schedule shop business, except that he has no any other source of income.
He has installed electricity to the shop premises and has been making payment of electricity bills to the concerned authority.
Thus, the plaintiff is in lawful possession and enjoyment of the suit schedule property.

The plaintiff further submits that the officials of the defendants without issuing prior notice to the plaintiff, all of a sudden along with their servants abruptly came to the property on 02.05.2014 and tried to demolish the shop of the plaintiff.
Somehow, he has thwarted their illegal acts.
The plaintiff has applied for allotment of shop to run his business, but still the plaintiff has not received any letter with regard to his request.
The defendants have flately refused for the same and threatened the plaintiff to dispossess him from the schedule premises.
Again on 22.11.2014, officials of the defendants came near to the shop along with the JCB and police authority and held out repeated threats of dispossession and demolition of the schedule shop.
The plaintiff lodged a complaint before the police.
Left with no alternative the plaintiff filed the instant suit.

sentences.text: After the service of suit summons, defendant No.1 appeared before court through his advocate - Smt.V.Prathima and defendant No.2 remained exparte.

The defendant No.1 - Commissioner, BBMP,
filed the written statement, denying the allegations made by the plaintiff against the defendants.
The said petty shop which the plaintiff has been erected on the footpath has not been covered by any permission from defendant No.1.

The plaintiff claims that he is physically handicapped and said to have been running a petty shop on the footpath by raising of loan from Syndicate Bank under SC/ST Scheme and he has been making repayment of EMI, he has installed electricity to his petty shop and making payment of electricity bills to the authorities concerned, are all not within the knowledge of the defendant.
The defendant No.1 submits that the plaintiff has not obtained prior permission of defendant No.1 for putting up petty shop on the foot path.
The claim of the plaintiff that permission to run the business of condiments has been granted by the authority concerned is of no consequence to the case on hand.
The defendant No.1 has directed the plaintiff to produce the copy permitting the erection of petty shop on the footpath, has failed to produce any such permission granted by defendant No.1.
Hence, the petty shop erected by the plaintiff is illegal and is liable to be removed.
Since the same is causing inconvenience to the pedestrians using the footpath.
The defendant No.1 has intimated the plaintiff regarding the intentions of removing the petty shop, which is obstructing the free flow of the pedestrians using the footpath.

The defendant No.1 contends that the plaintiff is of full knowledge regarding the drive taken by the defendant in view of directions issued by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka and the action taken by defendant No.1 is within the powers with defendant No.1 under Section 288(4) of KMC Act, 1976.
The allegation that along with police men and JCB, the defendants came near the spot and held threat of dispossession and demolition of petty shop etc., are all false.
The defendant No.1 is duty bound to revoke the encroachment made by the plaintiff on the footpath.
The suit itself is not maintainable and liable to be dismissed for non- compliance of mandatory provisions of Section 482 of KMC Act, 1976.
The plaintiff is guilty of suppressio veri and suggestio falsi and he has not approached the court with clean hands.
The plaintiff has brought the suit with malafide intention to prevent the defendants from exercising or doing their lawful duty.
There is no cause of action to file the suit and prayed that the suit be dismissed with costs.

4. Basing on the rival pleadings the following issues are framed:-
ISSUES 1.
Whether the plaintiff proves his lawful possession over the schedule shop premises as on the date of the suit?
2. Whether the plaintiff proves the alleged interference of the defendants?
3. Whether the plaintiff is entitled for the relief of permanent injunction?
4. What order or decree?
5. The plaintiff got himself examined as PW-1 and got examined his mother as PW-2 and got marked Ex.P1 to P3 and closed his side.

The defendants have not led any Sri.Thimmaraju.E vs The Commissioner on 18 July, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/153573389/
3 evidence.
6.
After the closure of the evidence, heard the arguments.

7. My answers to the above issues are as follows:-
 Issue No.1:- In the negative.
Issue No.2:- In the negative

. 
 Issue No.3:- In the negative.
Issue No.4:-
As per final order.

for the following:-
 REASONS

8. Issue No.1 to 3:-
For the sake of convenience these issues are taken up together for discussion to avoid repetition of facts and evidence.

The positive case of PW-1 is that, he is a physically handicapped person and has been running a petty shop, selling biscuits, bread, tea and other eatables since 20 years under the name and style Sri.Maruthi Condiment Shop, situated at Konanakunte Cross, near Bus Stop, Kanakapura Main Road, Bangalore, measuring 6 x 9 feet, morefully described in the suit schedule.

He has deposed in his evidence that he had obtained financial assistance from Syndicate Bank, Doddakalasandra Branch to the tune of Rs.3,00,000/- through SC/ST Scheme and has been making payment of EMI to the bank in respect of the loan borrowed by him.
Electricity installation was also made to the petty shop and he has been making payment of electricity bills to the concerned authority regularly.
It is his case that, since past 20 years he is in peaceful possession and enjoyment of the suit schedule property without any hindrance or disturbance from any one including the defendants.
He has stated in his evidence that the defendants had brought JCB and police to the spot and tried their level best to destroy the shop.
Somehow, he has thwarted such attempt made by the defendants.
Even he has lodged police complaint, but invain.
PW-2 his mother in her deposition has supported the case of the PW-1.

PW-1 has stated that such repeated incident took place on 22.11.2014 again,
public, go buyers and pedestrians enter to the spot and prevented the illegal and unlawful act of the defendants.
Therefore, it is the case of the plaintiff that, except running the said shop and derived income he doesn't have any other source of income.

To protect his possession over the suit schedule shop and also peacefully run the business, he apprehends danger from the hands of the defendants of their illegal interference, that is the reason he has approached this court seeking the remedy of permanent prohibitory injunction against them.
9. The plaintiff has produced Ex.P1 - Identity Card for Disabled issued by the competent authority and he is a physically disabled person can be gathered from this document.

Ex.P2 is the original Sri.Thimmaraju.E vs The Commissioner on 18 July, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/153573389/
4 voters ID of the plaintiff.
Ex . P3
- electricity bills paid by PW-1 to the KEB.

Merely, because the suit schedule shop was installed with the electricity connection and he has been making payment of electricity consumption charges and fact that he has obtained loan from Syndicate Bank,
Doddakalasandra Branch, Bangalore, for the purpose of running the business and has been making payment of EMI, doesn't create any right on the plaintiff to contend that the petty shop erected on the footpath without taking any license or permission from the defendants or local authorities and his possession is lawful.
Except these documents, he has not produced any other documents to substantiate his claim.
Though in the case file 2 photos are available, CD is not produced.
Even otherwise at glance it can be said that one petty shop was erected on the footpath itself.
10. The defendants have not denied the existence of the said petty shop on the footpath within the boundaries specified in the schedule of the plaint.
In the written statement itself it is clearly contended that defendant No.1 had directed the plaintiff to produce the copy permitting the erection of petty shop on the footpath.
But PW-1 has failed to produce any such permission granted by BBMP.
Even PW-1 has not made it clear that he had obtained license from BBMP before erecting the petty shop on the footpath.
The very pleading of the plaintiff itself manifestly makes it clear that he has erected the petty shop on the footpath.

If we see the photographs available on the spot, also shows that in front of the compound wall on the footpath portion by the side of the road he has put up such petty shop structure, of course it was a temporary structure.
Therefore, merely because as per his say since past 20 years he has been running his business in the said shop, doesn't create any right on him.
When the authorities have asked him to produce any permission or license given by the authority to put up such shop, he has not produced any documents before defendant No.1.
Even in this suit, he has not produced such documents.
Even he has not got marked the documents - a copy of Application for Registration under Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.
It is of little consequence as rightly contended by defendant No.1 to cloath the illegal erection of shop on the footpath with legality.

When evidence of PW-1 itself makes it clear that he has unauthorisedly,
without permission of BBMP, erected petty shop on the footpath portion of the road and has been running business, certainly it cannot be said that it is public premises.
The provisions of Karnataka Public Premises (Eviction of Unauthorised Occupants) Act, 1974, has no application as regards the suit property is concerned.

sentences.text:
11. The learned counsel for defendant No.1 has relied on a decision reported in 2009 (6) Kar.L.J.
453, in the case of V.Bramhananda v. Corporation of City of Mysore, Mysore and another, wherein it is held that if authority finds that temporary structure is causing inconvenience to public, it can refuse to renew license on its expiry and direct licensee to remove structure.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Footpath is not public premises and proceeding under the Karnataka Public Premises (Eviction of Unauthorised Occupants) Act is not required to be instituted for evicting licensee.

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: In various decisions of our own Hon'ble High Court, wherein a specific direction was issued to the local authorities, not to permit petty shop to be erected on the footpath, which would cause hardship to the pedestrians in general.
Therefore, the action taken by defendant No.1 - Commissioner, BBMP, was in exercise of the powers vested in him under Section 288 of KMC Act, 1976.

12. Even in certain cases where local authorities or BBMP grant permission to put up temporary structure and also issued license to run a shop, in case, if it is found that erection of such temporary Sri.

5 structure on the footpath create nuisance and problem for smooth movement of public at large and large number of public will be put to inconvenience, in such cases they even refuse to continue the said license and defendant No.1 is empower to evict such person by removing the structure erected on the footpath.

In the above said decision, it was held that the provisions of Karnataka Public Premises (Eviction of Unauthorised Occupants) Act, 1974, is not applicable to a temporary structure put up on the footpath.

Even the plaintiff has not made out in his pleadings or evidence that the provisions of Karnataka Public Premises (Eviction of Unauthorised Occupants) Act, 1974, has to be initiated against him.

sentences.text: His grievance is that, he is in lawful possession of the suit shop since past 20 years and running his business, he should not be forcibly dispossessed.
But, whether such acquitable relief is available for a person, who himself is guilty of erecting a temporary structure on the footpath, is a question.
Therefore, it is needless to say that he cannot claim that his possession is lawful.

Therefore, certainly BBMP is vested with necessary powers under the Act itself i.e., under Section 288(4) of KMC Act, 1976.
13.

The learned counsel for defendant No.1 has relied on another decision reported in 1986 (2)
Kar.L.J. 217, in the case Wajid.Y.S. & others v. State of Karnataka and others.

entities.text: Wajid.Y.S. & others v. State of Karnataka and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the above said case also it is held that the encroachment of any type, including of putting up any bunk shop is not permitted by statute itself and therefore, there is no power for the Corporation to permit to putting up any bunk shop on the footpath.
Here, defendant No.1 - BBMP had never issued any permission for PW-1 to put up bunk shop on footpath morefully mentioned in the plaint schedule.
PW-1 has not produced any documents worth to believe that he was permitted by defendant No.1 - BBMP to put up petty shop over footpath.
On the contrary, a specific pleading was there by defendant No.1 that they asked him to furnish any license or permission given to him by defendant No.1 to put up such temporary structure.
He has not furnished the same.
Therefore, it can be said that he is only a trespasser on footpath.
No doubt, he is a physically disabled and according to him he belongs to SC/ST, doesn't mean that under the garb of his disability he cannot violate the law.

Once it is not permitted to put up any temporary structure over footpath, which was meant for general public to use, by such act of erecting structure blocking the footpath which may create so many inconvenience and problems to the general public.
What is not permissible under law, if he is allowed to continue the same, certainly it amounts to misuse of process of law.

As such, the action taken by defendant No.1 to remove the temporary structure put up by PW-1 on the footpath is a statutory function carried by the authorities concerned in the interest of the public.
Even under the provisions of Specific Relief Act such statutory function lawfully carried out by the officials cannot be restrained by issuing order of injunction.

In the above said decision their lordships have held that the action taken by defendant No.1 under Section 288 (4) of KMC Act, 1976 is not oppose to Article 14, 21,
19(1)(g) of the Constitution.

The contention taken by the plaintiff was negatived by the Hon'ble High Court holding that the provisions contained in Section 288 of the Act are intended to meet the public needs and they are intended to be exercised in the interest of the public and to safeguard the public interest and also to ensure that no inconvenience is caused to the public in using the public roads and footpath.
The said provision was held as valid.

Therefore, it is needless to say that the erection of the petty shop by the plaintiff on the footpath itself is illegal and he cannot claim that he is in lawful possession and enjoyment of the property and without following due process of law he cannot be evicted.

The intended act taken by defendant No.1 was after being satisfied that the said petty shop put up on the footpath will cause inconvenience and problem to the general public in Sri.Thimmaraju.E vs The Commissioner on 18 July, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/153573389/
6 using the said road.

sentences.text:
14. Further more, the schedule property is situated at Konanakunte Cross, Near Bus Stop,
Kanakapura Main Road, Bangalore.

Nowadays, the vehicle traffic has been intensified on roads and equally due to rise in population it has become very difficult for the general public to have easy walk on the roads and they are facing so many inconvenience and threat to their life due to possible vehicular accident because of erection of such bunk shops, petty shops or allowing the hawkers to trade on the footpath itself.
To ensure the public safety if such action is taken by defendant No.1 under Section 288(4) of KMC Act, that cannot be said that they resorted to take illegal action arbitrarily.

The very photos produced by PW-1 which has not got marked but available in the file,
shows that existence of such petty shop certainly cause problems to pedestrians.

Therefore, the plaintiff cannot seek the relief of injunction against the defendants and in the larger interest of the general public, their safety, if such action is taken by the defendants to remove the obstruction caused for the smooth use of footpath by the general public, the said action is perfectly legal and authorities cannot be prevented by issuing an injunction.

15. Further PW-1 in his evidence had made allegations against the defendants that they came to the spot with JCB and police and threatened him of demolishing his shop, is not an act done by them arbitrarily.
On the contrary, it is necessary for the defendants to clear the footpath and road from any such obstructions for smooth vehicular traffic and movements by the people.
For that, if they come to the spot with the assistance of the police and JCB, the plaintiff cannot say that he apprehends danger to his property.
Because, the very putting up of such bunk shop on the footpath itself is illegal which doesn't confer any right on him, much less, he cannot claim that his possession is lawful.
He cannot say that he is in settled possession in the suit schedule property.

Therefore,
possessory remedy is not available for him.

Considering the larger interest of the people at large and their safety and the action taken by the defendants under Section 288 (4) of KMC Act is perfectly valid and such powers are vested in them and they exercised such powers for the public cause, that cannot be prevented by issuing an order of injunction.
Therefore, it is needless to say that the plaintiff is not entitled to get the relief of permanent prohibitory injunction against the defendants.

More over, he has not complied the mandatory provisions of Section 482 of KMC Act before filing this suit, even though considering his urgency this court has dispensed with issue of such notice, but question is that the plaintiff has not come before the court with clean hands, can be gathered from the evidence brought on record.
The erection of such bunk shop on the footpath without the permission of BBMP or license obtained from the local authorities itself is illegal.
Therefore, it is held that the plaintiff has failed to prove Issue No.1 and 2.

For the reasons discussed herein above in the considered view of this court, the plaintiff is not entitled to the relief of permanent injunction as prayed against the defendants and suit filed by the plaintiff against the defendants is liable to be dismissed.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.1 to 3 in the negative.

16. Issue No.4:- For the forgoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER Suit filed by the plaintiff against the defendants is hereby dismissed.
Under the circumstances, parties to bear their own costs.
